title: A short introduction to SHIP
text: build.target() constructs several targets. D F use data; G, Gpos, Gstar, cor also use pathway groups. diagonal target keeps sample variances sets covariances zero. constant-correlation target uses one average correlation -diagonal entries. knowledge-based targets restrict correlations genes share pathway; Gpos keeps positive links, Gstar separates positive negative links.
code: target_types <- c("D", "F", "G", "Gpos", "Gstar", "cor") targets <- setNames(   lapply(target_types, function(type) {     build.target(expl$x, expl$genegroups, type = type)   }),   target_types )  target_summary <- data.frame(   target = names(targets),   dimension = vapply(targets, function(target) paste(dim(target), collapse = " x "), character(1)),   nonzero = vapply(targets, function(target) sum(target != 0), integer(1)),   row.names = NULL ) target_summary #>   target dimension nonzero #> 1      D 100 x 100     100 #> 2      F 100 x 100   10000 #> 3      G 100 x 100    4028 #> 4   Gpos 100 x 100    2252 #> 5  Gstar 100 x 100    4028 #> 6    cor 100 x 100    3012

title: A short introduction to SHIP
text: target can passed shrink.estim(). value lambda close zero keeps empirical covariance matrix. value close one gives weight structured target. target definitions based Schaefer Strimmer (2005) Jelizarow et al. (2010), -optimism bioinformatics: illustration.
code: estimate <- shrink.estim(expl$x, targets[["G"]])  c(   lambda = estimate$lambda,   sample_variance = sum(diag(cov(expl$x))),   estimated_variance = sum(diag(estimate$shrink.cov)) ) #>             lambda    sample_variance estimated_variance  #>         0.04397249        24.93098682        24.93098682

title: Shrinkage estimator of the covariance matrix, given a data set and a covariance target. — shrink.estim
text: estimator combines sample covariance matrix \(S\) target matrix \(T\): $$\widehat{\Sigma} = \lambda T + (1 - \lambda)S$$ estimated intensity \(\lambda\) constrained \([0, 1]\). Values near zero keep sample covariance; values near one give weight target.

title: Knowledge-based constant-correlation target. — targetG
text: target applies constant-correlation model pairs genes share functional group. Let \(C = (c_{ij})\) binary group matrix let \(\bar{r}\) mean correlation among linked pairs. $$t_{ij} =   \begin{cases}     s_{ii} & \text{ } =j\\     \bar{r}\sqrt{s_{ii}s_{jj}} & \text{ } \neq j, \sim j   \end{cases}$$ \(\sim j\) means genes \(\) \(j\) share functional group. Unlinked -diagonal entries zero.
